verdict.rationale: Elicit's own Alerts feature continuously monitors topics for new papers and can email you instantly when one is found. A newer Routine feature, described on the Alerts legacy page, can act on what it finds by filtering, updating an artifact or writing a summary, which points to recurring agentic workflows rather than one-off runs. However, the evidence never documents user-defined schedules, cadence or a general job scheduler, so this is recurring monitoring rather than proven arbitrary scheduling. Missing for 10: explicit schedule/cadence configuration (e.g., daily/weekly), scheduling of arbitrary workflows such as Systematic Reviews or API jobs, detailed Routine documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: A Routine can act on what it finds and hand you a finished analysis: it can filter on criteria an Alert couldn't, update an artifact, or write the summary
Turn on **Instant email alerts** to be immediately alerted whenever a new relevant research paper is found.
Alerts keep you up to date on the latest research about topics that are relevant to you, ready to add to your Library for future use.
